karavīka.p: [Kala+ru+īka] (pu) CL=7 [Kalaṃ ravatīti karavīko, īko, la-lopo. Dhāna, ṭī. 626.] A bird cries a melodious sound. A Mythical bird (or) Indian cuckoo. Karavīka (Pu) [karavīka+ṇa. Karavīkasakuṇāvā bahavo ettha santīti karavīko. Dhāna, ṭī. 26.] Karavīka Mountain. A mountain where Mythical birds (or) Indian cuckoos live. This mountain is one of seven mountains that are surrounding Mount Myint Mo. See also - Karavīra.
pn: Karavīka. One of the seven mountains surrounding Sineru (Snp-a.ii.443; Vin-a.i.119; Vsm.206; Dhs-a.298). Between Karavīka and Īsādhara lay a Sīdantarasamudda. Ja.vi.125; see also Mvu.ii.300, where it is called Khadiraka, and Divy.217, 450.

karavīra.p: [Ku+ru+īra] (pu) CL=7 [Kucchitaṃ ravanti assā yena karavīro, īro. Dhāna, ṭī.577.] (1) A kind of flowering shrub resembling the periwinkle Cerbera Fruiticosa. (In dhāna, Sya, saca) it is an oleander tree. (2) Grass is named Karavīra. See - Karavīranāmaka. Karavīra(pu) [karavīra+ṇa. Ka+ru+īra] A mountain is called Karavīra. The oleander trees are dense and grow on this mountain. On these mountains, many Peacocks are crying the melodious sound.

[ကလ+ရု+ဤက။ ကလံ ရဝတီတိ ကရဝီကော၊ ဤကော၊ လ-လောပေါ။ ဓာန်၊ ဋီ။ ၆၂၆။]
P:
Karavīka，same J．V，204，416； Vv 364； Vism．112，206； VvA．166，219．

--bhāṇin speaking like the cuckoo，i．e．with a clear and melodious voice，one of the mahāpurisa-lakkhaṇas D．II，20=III，144=173=M．II，137，etc．； cp．Dial．II．17 n．and BSk．kalaviṅka-manojña-bhāṣin Sp．Av．Ś I．371 （Index p．225，where references to Lalitavist．are given）．（Page 196）
V:
Karavīka：One of the seven mountains surrounding Sineru （SnA．ii．443； Sp．i．119； Vsm．206； DhsA．298）．

Between Karavīka and Isādhara lay a Sīdantarasamudda．J．vi．125；

see also Mtu．ii．300，where it is called Khadiraka，and Divy．217，450．
